lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Rate of Change and Building Functions
lessonRef.focus: estimating rate of change from a graph
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: estimating rate of change from a graph

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A venue charges $90 to open plus $20 per attendee. Write C(n) for the total cost of n attendees, then find C(12).
Revenue is R(x) = 6x + 10 and cost is C(x) = -2x. Write the profit function P(x) = R(x) − C(x) in simplest form.
A table records output 22 at input 1 and output 29 at input 8. What is the average rate of change between these readings?
For f(x) = 2x² − 1x − 2, find the average rate of change from x = 5 to x = 4.
A sequence has g(1) = 9 and g(n) = 4·g(n − 1). Write the explicit form and find g(8).

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: A venue charges $75 to open plus $4 per attendee. Write C(n) for the total cost of n attendees, then find C(11).
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Revenue is R(x) = -2x − 2 and cost is C(x) = 7x. Write the profit function P(x) = R(x) − C(x) in simplest form.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A table records output 17 at input 1 and output -14 at input 5. What is the average rate of change between these readings?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
